newsitem.title: USA: Home Products Int'l adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Home Products Int'l adopts rights plan.

text.p: Home Products International Inc said Friday it adopted a shareholder rights plan and created staggered terms for members of its board.
The adoption of the rights plan was not spurred by any offer from an outside company for Home Products, said chairman and chief executive James Tennant.

Under the rights plan, the company declared a dividend of one preferred stock purchase right for each outstanding share of common stock. The dividend was scheduled to be paid to shareholders of record on August 20.

Each right entitles shareholders to purchase one-hundredth of a share of a new Series B junior participating preferred stock, with each fractional share of preferred stock equivalent in voting power to one share of Home Products' common stock. The rights would be exercisable only if a person or group becomes an "acquiring person" by becoming the owner of 15 percent or more of the company's stock, or announces a tender or exchange offer that would result in ownership of 15 percent or more of the company's shares, it said.

The board also adopted a proposal to create a "staggered" board of directors consisting of three classes of directors, each class being elected for a three-year term. The proposal will be presented to shareholders for approval at the next annual meeting in May.
